doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: The hot trumpet chair with Norvo and the Zudekoff brothers
summary: Looking at a 1938 band sheet, they discuss his 'hot' designation and the role of second trumpet versus first and third.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Now I’m looking at a sheet from a big band book, from 1938, and it has Red Norvo and it has you listed with Johnny Owens—
And you have an “H” after your name.
Hot. Hot trumpet. You were the hot man. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
Yeah. Now Barney Zudekoff, his brother was Moe Zudekoff, trombone player. Buddy Morrow, his name was Moe Zudekoff, Buddy Morrow. Okay.
Okay. So it wasn’t just the rock & roll guys who changed their names. So you went from Red Norvo, you were the hot chair, right? You were the guy that took the rides?

Second trumpet chair was always the ride chair. First trumpet just played first trumpet that’s what he did. Third trumpet player played third, and occasional easy first parts, so that the first trumpet player could take a break on the third part.
